metadata.title: Don't Use Fable 5 Broke
metadata.purpose: Teach viewers how to use Claude Fable 5 without burning through budget: short sessions, goal-first prompts, and a fast switch to Opus 4.8 for the rest of the work.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro) — durations are word-count estimates until GATE 0 audio lock

props.command: What is: Don't Use Fable 5 Broke?

beats.narration_text: Hei. This is Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude: how do I use Fable 5 without it costing a fortune? Here's what that looks like — because the model is pay-per-turn now, and most people are burning money on the very first message.

props.ask: How do I use Fable 5 without it costing a fortune?
props.answer_preview: Keep sessions short, lead with a goal, then switch to Opus…
props.command: Someone asked Claude: how do I use Fable 5 without it costing a fortune?

beats.narration_text: Fable 5 is the smartest AI model available right now — think of it as the senior lawyer who bills by the hour. Every turn you take, the bill grows, because Claude re-reads the entire conversation history at each exchange. The longer the chat, the faster costs compound. Two turns can be cheap. Forty turns is a problem.

illustration.concept: Two side-by-side cost curves. Left curve labeled 'Before': bill climbs steeply with each turn while results lag. Right curve labeled 'After': results spike fast in first two turns, bill stays flat. Style mirrors the Fable 5 infographic — hand-drawn on cream, terracotta dot marks the expensive 'Before' peak.
illustration.layout: Two equal panels side by side; x-axis labeled 'Turns', y-axis labeled 'Your Bill / Results'; terracotta accent on the Before bill curve only

beats.narration_text: The strategy is simple. Use Fable 5 for one or two turns maximum — give it a hard goal, not a task. Then switch to Opus 4.8 for everything else, because Opus is included in your subscription and, according to benchmarks at the time of writing, is cheaper and sharper than Sonnet 5.

card.sub: One hard goal. Then switch to Opus 4.8 for the rest.

beats.narration_text: Give it goals, not tasks. A task says: rewrite this email. A goal says: this client owes me two invoices and went quiet three weeks ago — here's the thread, goal is to get paid without burning the relationship, plan your approach and ask me what you don't know. Fable plans. It pushes back. It checks its own work before handing it to you. That is what the extra cost is for.

card.sub: Fable plans end-to-end. Tasks waste its ceiling.

beats.narration_text: An Anthropic engineer published four lines for talking to Fable. Line one: lead with the outcome — bottom line first, details after. Line two: only report work you can point to evidence for. Line three: say whether you want advice or action — Fable will write the email when you only wanted feedback on it. Line four: when you have enough information to act, act — give a recommendation, not a menu of options.

illustration.concept: Four numbered lines arranged as a sparse list on cream paper, hand-lettered. Each line has a short bold label (Lead with outcome / Evidence only / Advise vs Act / Decide don't survey) and one supporting phrase beneath. Terracotta accent on the line numbers only.
illustration.layout: Single column, left-aligned, generous leading between lines

beats.narration_text: The checklist from the infographic: pick one expensive problem, open a new chat, select Fable 5 on High, type your goal — not a task — add ask me questions first, answer first explain after, don't say done prove it. Stop after two messages. Switch to Opus 4.8. Finish the job there. Save it all in a Project.

card.sub: Hard goal · 2 turns max · Switch to Opus · Save in Project.

beats.narration_text: This week: find one decision you've been circling — a hire, a client to drop, a strategy choice. Open Fable 5, set effort to High, and type your goal in two sentences. Add: ask me questions first using the AskUserQuestion tool. Answer what it asks. Then switch to Opus 4.8 and finish. That is the full loop.

card.copy: Aim Fable at one hard decision
card.sub: Goal in two sentences. Ask-me-first. Switch to Opus after turn two.

beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Bear. Don't Use Fable 5 Broke. The model is elite — use it for two turns on your hardest problem, then hand off to Opus and let it finish.

card.sub: this is Liam, in for Bear

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this: you're using Claude with Fable 5 and something in your workflow broke after the update. Ask Claude to help you diagnose whether the breakage is a schema change, a behavior change, or a dependency issue — and show you the isolation test that tells you which it is without rewriting your whole workflow.
